_: Every number and name the game can be tuned with. docs/crawlers.xlsx is the AUTHORITY; this file is the default a fresh checkout builds from. build.py reconciles the two and refuses to build if a key exists in only one of them.

render.low_width.note: Internal render width. The picture is drawn this small, then scaled up with hard pixel edges to get the sprite look.

render.low_height.note: Internal render height. Keep the same shape as low_width (16:9) or the view letterboxes.

render.tile_w.note: Screen width of one 1m tile diamond at zoom 1.

render.tile_h.note: Screen height of one 1m tile diamond at zoom 1. Half of tile_w gives the classic 2:1 isometric view.

render.rise.note: How many pixels of screen height one metre of elevation is worth. Raise it to make the world feel taller and more vertical.

render.occluder_fade.note: How solid a block stays when it is standing between you and the tile you are inspecting. 1 = never fades, 0 = disappears entirely.

render.side_shade_left.note: Brightness of the left-facing wall of a block. Below 1 makes it darker than the top.

render.side_shade_right.note: Brightness of the right-facing wall of a block.

render.height_tint.note: How much lighter a surface gets per metre of elevation. Gives depth without lighting.

camera.zoom_max.note: Closest in you can zoom. Whole numbers only, so pixels stay square. Zooming in shows fewer metres, not more detail.

camera.key_pan_speed.note: How fast the arrow keys slide the view.

world.chunk_tiles.note: Width and depth of the piece of labyrinth generated. 28 tiles = 28 metres across.

world.max_elevation.note: Tallest the ground is allowed to get above the floor of a chunk.

world.terrain_scale.note: Size of the lumps in the ground. Bigger = broader, smoother hills; smaller = choppier.

world.ramp_chance.note: How often a one-metre step gets a ramp instead of being a wall you cannot climb.

world.damp_level.note: At or below this elevation the ground is wet. Water and moss appear here.

roll.attribute_weight.note: How much a natural attribute is worth in a roll. A 10 in the attribute is worth 30 with this at 3.

roll.skill_weight.note: How much practice is worth in a roll. At 1, a skill of 100 is worth 100 -- practice eventually outweighs talent.

roll.noise_spread.note: How much luck swings a single attempt, either way. Lower makes the better character win more reliably.

skill.cap.note: The most practice any one skill can hold.

learn.gain_on_failure.note: Practice gained from a FAILED attempt. Rule 1: failing is how a character learns.

learn.gain_on_success.note: Practice gained from a successful attempt. Deliberately small -- succeeding teaches you very little.

learn.near_miss_bonus.note: Extra practice for only just failing. Getting close teaches most of all.

learn.near_miss_margin.note: How close a failure has to be to count as only just missing.

actor.count.note: How many crawlers start in the chunk.

actor.attribute_min.note: Lowest a natural attribute can be rolled at. Ordinary people sit near 10.

actor.attribute_max.note: Highest a natural attribute can be rolled at.

actor.hat_chance.note: How many crawlers turn up already wearing something on their head.

actor.step_ticks.note: How long a crawler pauses between attempts to move. 60 ticks is a second.

actor.height_m.note: How tall a grown crawler is. One tile is one metre, so this is how tall they look.

world.metres_per_tile.note: READ ONLY. One tile is one square metre. Non-negotiable rule 7.

render.iso_ratio.note: READ ONLY. tile_w divided by tile_h. Changing this is changing the camera, not balancing the game.

figure.nominal_height_m.note: READ ONLY. The height the figure tab's part measurements are written against. A crawler of a different height has every part scaled by the same ratio.

ui.hint_desktop.text: drag to pan  ·  scroll to zoom  ·  hover anything to inspect it

ui.hint_touch.text: drag to pan  ·  pinch to zoom  ·  tap anything to inspect it

character.name_pool.text: Bran, Ysolde, Corwin, Maerl, Thessa, Odric, Vela, Garn, Ketta, Rhodry, Isme, Dunmar, Sable, Wren, Halgar, Nix, Orla, Tam, Brennis, Sorrel

floor.name: floor
floor.note: A surface something can stand on.

solid.name: solid
solid.note: Fills its metre. Nothing walks through it.

ramp.name: ramp
ramp.note: Climbs exactly one metre between levels.

stone.name: stone
stone.note: Made of worked or natural rock.

water.name: water
water.note: Standing water. Shallow enough to wade.

damp.name: damp
damp.note: Wet underfoot. Things rot and grow here.

unstable.name: unstable
unstable.note: Loose. Shifts when weight is put on it.

grim.name: grim
grim.note: A reminder of what happened here.

person.name: person
person.note: A thinking creature with the six attributes and skills of its own.

crawler.name: crawler
crawler.note: One of yours: came into the labyrinth, may yet leave it.

stone_floor.name: Stone Floor
stone_floor.note: Worked flagstone. The default footing of the labyrinth.

moss_stone.name: Mossy Stone
moss_stone.note: Stone gone green where the water sits.

shallow_water.name: Shallow Water
shallow_water.note: Ankle deep. Slows a walker, ruins what it soaks.

stone_block.name: Stone Block
stone_block.note: A full cubic metre of rock.

might.name: Might
might.note: Raw physical force. Lifting, hauling, forcing, and the heavy end of any tool.

agility.name: Agility
agility.note: Speed and fine control. Keeping your feet, quick hands, delicate work.

endurance.name: Endurance
endurance.note: Staying power. Long marches, cold nights, illness, a whole day of work.

presence.name: Presence
presence.note: Effect on other people. Singing, teaching, calming a panic, bargaining.

intellect.name: Intellect
intellect.note: What can be learned and worked out. Recipes, repairs, maps, lore.

willpower.name: Willpower
willpower.note: What can be made to happen anyway. Fear, pain, boredom, sticking at a hated task.

clambering.name: Clambering
clambering.note: Keeping your feet on bad ground: water, rubble, moss, a steep ramp. Rolled every time a crawler tries to step onto a difficult tile.

torso.name: Torso
torso.note: Always drawn. The cloth colour, and the widest part of a crawler.

hat.name: Hat
hat.note: Only drawn on a crawler wearing one. Keep half_width near the head's or the brim hides the face. Rule 4: if it is on them, it is on screen -- add a row here and it can be worn.
